S2_BUDGET_DEFINITION.why: the measured artefact is 334,778 UTF-8 bytes over 237 atoms = 1,412.6 B/atom, so the absolute 20,000-byte bound is equivalent to 14.2 atoms and could never be met by a corpus of this size; the corpus is 16.7x the bound's implied envelope and removing all known lossless duplication floors at 263,653 B, still 13.2x over. A scale-invariant rate is the same protection stated in a form that a growing corpus cannot falsify by construction.
S2_BUDGET_DEFINITION.note: no numeric threshold was raised or lowered. The 20,000-byte absolute row remains measured and printed. What changed is which row decides.

S2_TIMING_THRESHOLDS.why: measured headroom 2.35x / 1,579x / 51x. They cannot fire, carry no signal, and were diluting the discriminating power of the hard gate. They stay measured and printed; they no longer vote.

S2_HISTORICAL_FAIL.how: kept as a non-voting ADVISORY row with verdict FAIL, re-emitted in the `historical.preserved_fails` block of every --check run. It is measured, printed and never rewritten.

S2_REGRESSION_GUARD.what: bytes_per_atom is compared against a frozen baseline (tolerance 10%) and FAILs on regression
S2_REGRESSION_GUARD.why: this is the mechanism that actually protects the property the old absolute number was trying to protect: the artefact must not grow per unit of requirement.

S2_LOSSLESS_DEDUP.what: the same clause text is stored three times (source_clause.text 6,755 B + oracle.predicate 6,755 B + failure_condition 10,085 B = 23,595 B); row-constant fields repeat per row
S2_LOSSLESS_DEDUP.why: it is a legitimate cleanup but it is NOT sold as closing any budget; the FAR measured that even fully applied it reaches only 263,653 B. Executing it would change the artefact contract and every consumer, which is out of this round's scope.
